title: Collecting Chocolates
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of size n, where nums[i] represents the cost of collecting the chocolate of the ith type, you can perform an operation that changes the type of all chocolates of the ith type to the (i + 1) % n type, incurring a cost of x for each operation.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of size n, where nums[i] represents the cost of collecting the chocolate of the ith type, you can perform an operation that changes the type of all chocolates of the ith type to the (i + 1) % n type, incurring a cost of x for each operation. The task is to determine the minimum total cost required to collect chocolates of all types.
constraints: Chocolate type i initially costs nums[i].
Pay x for one global cyclic operation; after k operations, type i may be bought using any of the k+1 cyclically preceding prices.
Choose the operation count and one purchase price per type to minimize total cost.
hints: There are only n distinct useful rotation counts.
Maintain each type’s cheapest reachable price as one more cyclic source becomes available.
For every k from zero through n-1, minimize sum(best prices)+k*x.
For a fixed k, choosing each type’s cheapest reachable price is independent; enumerating every useful k therefore includes the global optimum.

tests.explanation: After two rotations every type can use price one, so purchases cost three and rotations cost ten, totaling thirteen.
Rotations cannot save their cost, so buying immediately costs six.
